General Information Authority The 2014 Quadrennial Defense Review (QDR) established innovation as a central line of effort in the national defense strategy of the United States. The decisive military advantage of the United States over its adversaries and peer competitors is steadily eroding. Consequently, under 10 U.S.C. 3458, Contracting Officers may acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services using a competitive procedure called a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). cle protection for years to come. Leverage Government Investment: Utilize provided TDPs to accelerate development and reduce risk. Become a Key Partner: Establish a strong relationship with the GVSC and the U.S. Army. We invite qualified organizations with expertise in hardware development, firmware integration, and MOSA principles to submit proposals for delivery of 10 VBK prototypes, with a follow-on option to deliver additional kits. The signatures being requested include thermal, acoustic, and radio frequency, but others will also be considered. The technologies may be applique or coatings. The suite of equipment on a CL flightline must be rapidly deployed to support sortie generation (missions to attack an enemy position and return to the CL or another base). The elements of support can include, but are not limited to, aircraft power, conditioned air, refueling, rearming, and diagnostic and recovery tasks. To maximize flexibility, it’s desirable for the equipment to be multi-fuel capable (if fuel is required) and energy efficient to reduce the risk to operations from contested fuel logistics and to limit fuel pre-positioning requirements. In addition, it’s desirable for the equipment to support force sustainment elements, including human performance, low maintenance, and the wellbeing of the user. The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this Request for Quotation (RFQ) to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the RFQ and represents the overall Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government, price and other factors considered. LPTA is determined by evaluating all non-cost proposals on an "acceptable vs. unacceptable" basis. Once a quotation meets the minimum objective standards deﬁned in the solicitation, the contract is awarded to the offeror with the lowest evaluated price, with no additional value given for exceeding technical requirements. To be eligible for award, the offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at SAM.gov, have current representations and certiﬁcations, and not be listed on the SAM exclusions list. The Government will review each offeror's price and order them from lowest to highest priced. The Government will evaluate quotations in ascending price order until a minimum of two (2) quotations are determined to be Technically Acceptable. Under the LPTA approach, the Government will evaluate the three (3) lowest quotes up front if more than 3 offerors are received. This source selection will evaluate the lowest-price quote ﬁrst for technical acceptability, if it passes, the award will be made;

n Antonio, Randolph Air Force Base (JBSA-Randolph) aircraft hangars. Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An inoperable fan system poses a significant threat to both personnel (heat-related injuries) and sensitive aircraft components. This contract proactively maintains the integrity and safety of these vital hangar environments and mitigates the risks associated with equipment failure. 1.0 SCOPE. forms_signatures.text: . 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. The government will neither supervise contractor employees, nor control the methods the contractor performs the required tasks, nor prepare work schedules for individual contractor employees; however, the contractor shall consider the Government’s duty hours and work schedule. If the contractor feels that any actions constitute or are perceived to constitute personal services, the contractor shall notify the Contractor Officer (CO) immediately. 2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS. The contractor shall comply with the following documents and standards in the performance of this contract: • Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Maintenance and Safety Manuals • National Electrical Code (NEC) Standards • Air Force Occupational Safety and Health (AFOSH) Standards • National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Standards • Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) and applicable ETL fire safety standards 3.0 REQUIREMENT 3.1 Annual Preventative Maintenance. The Contractor shall perform annual preventive maintenance (PM) on all twenty-one (21) fans during each period of performance. To ensure standardized annual intervals, the Contractor shall execute the required PM event no earlier than four (4) months and no later than seven (7) months into the period of performance. The aptitudes and abilities measured by the ASVAB include General Science, Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge, Electronics Information, Auto Information, Shop Information, Mechanical Comprehension, and Assembling Objects. Test takers receive a standardized score from 1-100 for each of these subtests. The Army combines scores on the ASVAB subtests into composites, also known as aptitude areas (AAs) or line scores, to determine eligibility into each initial-entry MOS. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. The Army combines scores on the ASVAB subtests into composites, also known as aptitude areas (AAs) or line scores, to determine eligibility into each initial-entry MOS. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. Effective classification and assignment of Soldiers is dependent on being able to discriminate the different abilities of Soldiers based on how well they score on the AA composites of the ASVAB. The overarching objective of this effort is to conduct research to determine if the Army would benefit from updated AA composites used to determine MOS fit. The current project aims to identify potential redundancy within the current ASVAB AA composites,

The multi-domain operations (MDO) concept requires Army teams to operate semi-independently but also to utilize the capabilities across multiple domains to conduct sustained missions in highly contested environments. Additionally, high personnel turnover for teams is expected in the FOE as casualty counts increase, rapid teaming is required, and ad hoc teams become common. Within the literature, creativity has been conceptualized and examined as both an antecedent (e.g., Yang & Hung, 2021; Zhang & Bartol, 2010) and an outcome (e.g., Liu et al., 2022; Tierney & Farmer, 2011). In a recent review by Lua et al. (2024), the authors discuss creativity behaviors like idea implementation, innovative behavior, and personal initiative. Teng et al. (2020) examined the relationship between creative self-efficacy and innovative behavior. In the study, the authors used Scott and Bruce’s (1994) measure of innovative behaviors which includes items such as “generates creative ideas” and “develops adequate plans and schedules for the implementation of new ideas” (p. 607). For the purpose of this effort, we are interested in creativity as an outcome and, more specifically, creative performance with technology. Creativity research is not novel to the U.S. Army, but largely exists at the antecedent level. Two previous job analysis projects included innovation and creativity in surveys of talent requirements (Boyle et al., 2022) and personnel characteristics (Royston & Lin, 2022) across military occupational specialties (MOS). Additional ARI efforts have examined divergent thinking (Russell et al., 2017) and creative thinking (Zaccaro et al., 2012). Results for these reports indicate the importance of creativity across MOS and ranks but are not specific to creative performance behaviors with technology. 4 The purpose of this project is to develop and validate a measure of creative performance with technology. WHITE PAPER TOPIC: Refinement of the Common Cyber Capabilities Assessment A promising strategy to meet the increasing Cyber personnel demands is to select entry-level staff with little or no formal information technology education, but high potential, and then make investments in training. One means to identify high-potential candidates for training is to build a measure of the skills and abilities most typically associated with success across the military Cyber jobs. Cyber training for enlisted Soldiers is lengthy, challenging, and requires significant investment from the Army. The necessity of Cyber jobs has led to an increasing demand for quality personnel. By assessing the underlying skills and abilities associated with success in Cyber work, the Army can identify high- potential candidates, meet the increasing demand for these personnel, more accurately predict performance, and reduce attrition during the training process. To aid in identification of high-potential candidates for Cyber training, the Army Research Institute (ARI) developed the Common Cyber Capabilities assessment (C^3).

ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION 3.1 ELIGIBLE PROPOSERS All responsible sources capable of satisfying the Government’s needs may submit a proposal to this ISO. Specifically, universities, non-profit organizations, small businesses and other than small businesses are eligible and encouraged to propose to this ISO. Early career investigators are preferred. While there is statutory language that may suggest ARPA-H is limited in the number of awards it may make to one entity, there are circumstances in which ARPA-H may make more than three (3) awards to a particular person or entity. ARPA-H encourages entities to submit their research ideas notwithstanding

ons in accordance with applicable federal law, including the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). 5 SUBMISSION REVIEW AND EVALUATION PROCESSES 5.1 CONFORMING SUBMISSIONS Conforming submissions contain all requirements detailed in this ISO. Submissions that fail to include required information may be deemed non -conforming and may be removed from further consideration and/or rejected without further review . A submission may be deemed non-conforming under this ISO if it fails to meet one or more of the following solicitation requirements: • The proposed concept is applicable to the BRAINS Exploratory Topic. • The proposers meet the eligibility requirements. • The submission meets the submission requirements. • The submission meets the content and formatting requirements in the attached instructions. • The proposer’s concept has not already received funding or been selected for award negotiations for another funding opportunity (whether from ARPA -H or another Government agency). Proposers will be notiﬁed of non-conforming determinations via email correspondence. Please note that ARPA -H reserves the right, at its discretion, to reject as non -conforming ARPA-H-SOL-26-148, BRAINS 13 proposals that it determines are duplicative of previously submitted solution summaries

THE EXPLORATORY TOPIC BRAINS is an Exploratory Topic with two (2) intake groups, each will take 18 months from kickoff to completion and will consist of two (2) 9-month phases with a down select at the end of Phase 1. Criteria for moving to Phase 2 are the metrics as described in Tables 2, 3, and 4 for Phase 1. 2.1 Technical Areas (TAs) and Milestones Using natural brain development as a blueprint, BRAINS will seed efforts for two (2) technical areas, which are essential for later steps in functionally replacing damaged brain tissue. In TA1 teams will design developmental mim icking or tissue engineering methods capable of generating precursor tissue for a part of the brain other than neocortex . In TA2 teams will provide proof-of-concept for surgical engraftment into adult brains of non -human fetal precursor tissues for their selected brain area. Teams must propose to address all milestones and metrics of either one TA or both. TA1: Defining and generating precursor tissue

The Contractor shall include all labor, supervision, management, materials, equipment, tools, vehicles, transportation, licenses, permits, certifications, overhead, profit, and incidentals necessary to perform the requirements of each CLIN within the fixed price proposed and awarded. The CLIN structure is intended to provide pricing visibility for major service areas while maintaining the Firm-Fixed-Price nature of the contract. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to award a service-based contract for landscape and grounds maintenance for the VA Central California Health Care Systems (VACCHCS). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 561730, with a small business size standard of $9.5 Million. This acquisition is being conducted as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business set-aside. The anticipated period of performance will consist of a base period with four (4) option years, as identified in the solicitation documents. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular. The full solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement and attachments, is included with this posting. Offerors are responsible for monitoring this site for amendments or updates. A este respecto, indicar que la dirección competente ha de regirse por un Sistema de Gestión de Calidad basado en la norma ISO 9000-2015, tal y como establece su Convenio Colectivo y que, naturalmente, se audita. Las actividades realizadas y el cumplimiento de la normativa descrita serán validados por la Dirección competente de la Agencia en materia de formación, comunicación y gestión del cambio.DEFINICIÓN DEL PLAN DE FORMACIÓNEl adjudicatario desarrollará un Plan de Formación atendiendo a los hitos establecidos en el Plan de Proyecto o en la ejecución de cualquiera de los servicios objeto del pliego, y deberá ser presentado a la Agencia con laantelación suficiente para que esté validado antes de que se inicie la fase de implantación. El Plan de Formación deberá inclui

vas.iv.Ámbito y Perfiles de Formación, distinguiendo entre:Usuarios de la Comunidad de Madrid, con sus diferentes perfilesEmpleados de la Agencia, con sus diferentes perfiles (mantenimiento legal, correctivo y evolutivo, soporte y atención a los usuarios, formadores, etc.)La formación se llevará a cabo, preferentemente en las instalaciones de la Agencia. No obstante, el adjudicatario tendrá que tener disponibilidad de las instalaciones que sean necesarias para el desarrollo de las acciones formativas planificadas, si así se lo requiere la Agencia.Dichas instalaciones deberán cumplir con la normativa relativa al Sistema de Gestión de Calidad (ISO 9001:2008),y así mismo, deberán estar ubicadas en una zona céntrica y bien comunicada de Madrid. Las instalaciones propuestas deberán tener todos los elementos necesarios para la impartición de las acciones formativas (fundamentalmente en lo que atañe a los equipos informáticos, instalaciones y mobiliario, accesibilidad y aspectos básicos de seguridad). umple con los objetivos de continuidad de negocio definidos en el proyecto Nexus.Transparencia para el usuario: Cambio entre CPDs sin interrupciones perceptibles.Gracias a la replicación activa y a los mecanismos de conmutación automática (failover), el traspaso de operaciones entre CPDs se realiza de forma imperceptible para los usuarios. Esto garantiza una Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 261 de 329 experiencia fluida y sin degradación del rendimiento, incluso durante eventos críticos o mantenimientos programados.Seguridad reforzada: Cumplimiento de estándares internacionales.El Geocluster incorpora prácticas alineadas con normativas como ISO 27001 y NIST, asegurando la protección de datos y la resiliencia ante ciberataques. La redundancia y la sincronización constante contribuyen a minimizar riesgos asociados a pérdida de información o accesos no autorizados.Flexibilidad operativa: Mantenimientos sin impacto en la carga productiva.Al contar con servidores activos en más de un CPD, es posible realizar intervenciones técnicas, actualizaciones o pruebas en uno de los centros sin afectar la operación global. Esto optimiza la gestión de recursos, reduce ventanas de mantenimiento y mejora la eficiencia del equipo técnico.*** FIN DEL ANEXO 7 *** Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 262 de 329 ANE

deliverables_scope.text: al que presta el sistema y cuya justificación obedece a cuestiones de diferente naturaleza: Factores tecnológicos: Arquitectura totalmente basada en SAP , incluyendo núcleo transaccional, integraci ones, analítica y experiencia de usuario.Con integraciones críticascon más de 40 sistemas externos, que deberían rehacerse por completo si se cambiara la tecnología. Modelos de datos y procesos financieros especializados , alineados con estándares SAP y con la normativa económico-presupuestaria de la Comunidad de Madrid. Altísima complejidad técnica y funcional, que exige conocimiento experto exclusivamente en SAP. Evolución continua de gran volumen conforme a cambios normativos y requerimientos de centros gestores construida bajo una base tecnológica robusta y contrastada SAP Inversiones recientes vigentes en licencias on-premise y cloud (expedientes 2024 2025) que deben ser aprovechadas. Factores operativos Continuidad del servicio: mantener la solución tecnológica basada en SAP garantiza el mantenimiento y evolución de este servicio público esencial que afecta a la gestión de ingresos, pagos, presupuesto, contabilidad, compras, logística y contratación de toda la Comunidad de Madrid. Gestión homogénea para los 12.000 usuarios del sistema y aseguramiento de la trazabilidad e i

lizada a través de la Oficina de Proyecto y Producto, estructurada en torno a buenas prácticas SAP. Factores económicos Maximización de la inversión pública realizada durante más de 15 años en licencias, parametrización, desarrollos, integraciones y formación. Aprovechamiento de licencias y suscripciones adquiridas, cuyo coste ya ha sido asumido en expedientes recientes. Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026 Página 5 de 12 Evitar un coste muy elevado de sustitución, dado que cambiar de plataforma obligaría a reimplantar desde cero todos los procesos, suponiendo además incurrir en costes redundantes por duplicación de sistemas de gran complejidad y volumetría de gestión Prevención de sobrecostes normativos , ya que SAP incorpora actualizaciones estándar alineadas con normativa de contabilidad y contratación. La continuidad de NEXUS ECCL sobre tecnología SAP es la opción más eficiente, segura, sostenible y alineada con las inversiones realizadas y los requisitos del servicio público. Un cambio tecnológico supondría riesgos y sobrecostes injustificables, comprometiendo la operativa económico-financiera de la Comunidad de Madrid. Para ello, además, como se ha mencionado, será pieza fundamental la dotación del servicio de una Oficina de Proyecto y Producto que coordine la gobernanza, la defi

El Encargado del Tratamiento(ET)es la persona física o jurídica, autoridad pública, servicio u otro organismo que trata datos personales por cuenta del RT, que en la práctica se traduce en que ejecuta el encargo recibido del RT con sujeción a las directrices que éste le ha trasladado (aunque pueda eventualmente disponer de un cierto margen de decisión). En el presente pliegoel ET se apoya en un tercero, la empresa adjudicataria,que actuará en calidad deSubencargado del Tratamiento (SubET):x La Agencia para la Administración Digital de la Comunidad de Madrid, que actuará como Encargado del Tratamiento.x La empresa adjudicataria, que actu

eción a las directrices que éste le ha trasladado (aunque pueda eventualmente disponer de un cierto margen de decisión). Pakkuja meeskonna pädevus Tehnilise kirjelduse punktides 11.1–11.4 sätestatud rollide, kompetentsivaldkondade ja keelenõuete olemasolu kontrollitakse pakkumuse vastavuse hindamisel. Kvaliteedihindamisel ei hinnata nende miinimumnõuete täitmist uuesti, vaid võrreldakse nõuetele vastavate meeskondade kogemuse ulatust ja asjakohasust, rollijaotuse läbimõeldust, kompetentside täiendavust ning võimekust rakendada neid kompetentse käesoleva teenuse osutamisel. Hindamise aluseks on pakkumuse vastavuse kontrolli läbinud meeskonna ülevaade, meeskonnaliikmete CV-d ning pakkumuses esitatud projektide, lepingute või muude kogemust tõendavate tööde kirjeldused. Hinnatakse: meeskonna koosseisu, liikmete rolle ning ülesannete ja vastutuse jaotust; teenuse- või elamusmajanduse mudeli protsesside kavandamise ja läbiviimise kogemuse ulatust ning asjakohasust; turismitoodete või külastuselamuste arendamise kogemuse ulatust ning asjakohasust; ettevõtjate praktilise koolitamise ja mentorluse kogemuse ulatust ning asjakohasust; koostööpõhiste toodete, võrgustike või partnerlusmudelite arendamise kogemuse ulatust ning asjakohasust; rahvusvahelise turismimüügi, reisikorraldajate vajaduste või välisturule sisenemi

kohasust; prototüüpimise, kasutaja- või klienditestimise ja tagasiside põhjal iteratsioonide juhtimise kogemuse ulatust ning asjakohasust; meeskonnaliikmete kompetentside omavahelist täiendavust ja rakendamist käesoleva teenuse osutamisel. ip_data_security.text: ncluding fixed-price incentive fee contracts. 1.2 Background The U.S. Army recognizes that investments in producibility and advanced manufacturing, as well as existing capabilities will need to continue to be made to support a vast array of cru- cial activities, including but not limited to acquisition, sustainment, logistics, and ultimately the Army’s Modernization of its Organic Industrial base (OIB). In order to deliver impactful operational results, the U.S. Army must modernize the OIB, particularly in the areas of agile / flexible facilities, connected digital enterprise, advanced manufacturing, Digital Twin, auto- mation, and cyber security. DEVCOM has coined these technologies collectively as Conver- gent Manufacturing. Additionally, Watervliet Arsenal is looking for modified existing commercial technologies, services, and concurrent manufacturing; in an effort to ensure no drop in capabilities and pro- ducibility. With the focus on both “new capabilities”, “modified existing capabilities”, and “opera- tional constructs” convergent manufacturing technologies will accelerate the OIB’s capability to get generalized and advanced solutions to the Warfighter while enhancing and optimizing the Defense Manufacturing Base for today and tomorrow’s missions. July 2026 CUI CUI Statement of Work (SOW) Briefing Rooms Seating 1.0 OBJECTIVE 1.1 Military Training Operations (MTO) is requesting procurement and installation of 305 new auditorium seats. The Contractor shall supply all necessary personnel, equipment, supplies, tools, trucks, supervision, and services for procuring and installing auditorium seating at bldg. 7310 Phantom Street, Keesler Air Force Base, Mississippi 39534. 1.2 MTO will not accept damaged furniture or equipment to be installed. The Contractor shall be responsible for replacing any damaged items and removing all packaging materials/debris upon completion. 2.0 REQUIREMENTS 2.1 DESCRIPTION OF WORK 2.1.2 Seating • The seating area is in three different locations of bldg.7310. The first location of 60 seats is on the main floor (Room 152), requiring no stairs or elevators. Room 152 is 36 ½ ft x 23 ft and will need to have 6 rows of 5 seats interlocked on both side of the center aisle. The second location (Room 220) of 175 seats is on the second floor and has either stairs or elevator access. Room 220 is 39 ft x 65 ft and will need to have 12 rows with 10 seats interlocked and 5 rows with 11 seats interlocked divided on both sides of the room along the center aisle. The Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certiﬁcation (CMMC) is a framework for assessing a contractor's compliance with applicable information security protections (see 32 CFR part 170). (c) Duplication. The CMMC assessments will not duplicate efforts from any other comparable DoD assessment, except for rare circumstances when a reassessment may be necessary, for example, when there are indications of issues with cybersecurity and/or compliance with CMMC requirements. (d) Requirements. Q: Does the requirement mandate a 100% vendor-furnished rental model, or does SAVAHCS retain any existing Customer-Owned Linen Items (COLI) that the contractor will be required to process alongside rented inventory? A: A 100% vendor-furnished rental model. Q: If COLI processing is required, will the vendor be held liable for standard wear-and- tear or replacement costs for government-owned items? A: No. Q: What is the exact required Par level distribution across the health care system prior to Day 1 of contract performance (e.g., 3-Par, 4-Par, or 5-Par systemwide)? A: 3 Days. Q: What is the breakdown of initial Par stock required on-site at the SAVAHCS main campus versus off-site reserve? A: Off Site Reserve will be 96 hour contingency linen. Q: Will the VA provide an explicit physical technical specification sheet (e.g., thread count, GSM weight, fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding, surgical drape fluid-resistance ratings) for each line item? A: Fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding depending on the cost. 36C26227Q0001 Page 5 of 11 Q: Are micro-fiber mop heads, microfiber cloths, and barrier isolation gowns included in the general 1,350,000 lbs annual estimated volume, or are they counted / tracke

requirements, and designated delivery time slots for each satellite location. A: N/A. Q: Is the contractor required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts, poly-dump carts, and wire delivery hampers? A: Contractor is required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts. 36C26227Q0001 Page 6 of 11 Q: What are the physical dimensional constraints (height, width, depth) of the SAVAHCS logistics staging area, freight elevators, and clean linen rooms to ensure incoming contractor carts fit properly? A: Average dock dimensions for 24-foot box truck. Q: What is the minimum quantity of dedicated exchange carts required to remain on-site at SAVAHCS at all times? A: 30. Q: Is contractor performance restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange, or is the contractor responsible for internal ward-level replenishment / clean linen room stocking? A: Restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange. Main Street Winston-Salem, NC 27155 Winston-Salem Regional Office Online Career Assessment and Portal 1. Introduction The Winston-Salem Regional Office (WSRO), Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E) Division requires the continued use of an online career assessment system. Currently, the WSRO is using the Career Occupational Preference System (COPSystem) career assessment to assist VR&E counselors with the assessment of a Veteran’s abilities, interests and work values. The online assessment is a managed service and runs on any computer with Internet access. The assessment requires no software instal

r satisfaction, the WSRO would prefer to continue the use of the COPSystem rather than use and learn a new system. 1.1 Scope The scope of services includes The online career assessment software provides a tailored path of career and education options for veterans. COPS software quickly measures both interest, abilities and work values through reliable assessment tasks. The Edits, Inc. is the sole publisher and sole source of the following products, all of which are proprietary, patented, and copyrighted. 1.2 Period of Performance The period of performance is for one base year from the date of award with four option years. 2. General Requirements This section describes the general requirements for this effort. The career testing should be a commercially available “off-the-shelf” online subscription service. The career assessment should assess a Veteran’s vocational abilities/aptitudes, interests and work values. The career assessment must have established reliability, validity and normed data substantiating its efficacy and accuracy. The career assessment should have an online portal that is accessible by both Veteran and VR&E staff via the internet. The contract should allow the purchase of additional assessments during the contract year if the need exists to serve VR&E Veterans.

COPS software quickly measures both interest, abilities and work values through reliable assessment tasks. This includes conducting compliant risk assessments, routine vulnerability scanning, system patching and change management procedures, and the completion of an acceptable contingency plan for each system. The Center for Army Analysis (CAA) seeks proposals for an innovative Information Technology (IT) services solution to enhance agency-wide IT and desktop support across its internally managed classified Closed Restricted Network (CRN) and its externally managed classified and unclassified network environments. Offerors shall provide a detailed narrative demonstrating their organizational capacity and a proven record of delivering effective, efficient support services comparable in scope to this requirement. The narrative must include specific examples of service delivery models, internal quality control measures, and a summary of historical performance metrics achieved for clients of comparable size and complexity. The term innovative is defined as any technology, process, or method, including research and development that is new as of the date of proposal submission, or any new application of an existing technology, process or method as of the proposal date. Offerors are encouraged to submit multiple options. The Government reserves the right to extend this CSO beyond the open until date by amendment if the authority is extended. Under this CSO, the DoD may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches, and/or proposals from traditional and nontraditional business entities for innovative commercial products, technologies, and services, or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial products, technologies, and services to meet U.S. Army needs and improve readiness. These include, but are not limited to, IT modernization, enhanced cybersecurity, efficient artifact restoration and conservation, streamlined base operations, and improved facility support. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include, but are not limited to, commercially-available products, technologies, or services immediately available; commercially-available products, technologies, or services fueled by commercial or strategic investment; and concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial products, technologies, or services, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. The G

ars have been reserved for awards under this CSO. The participating DoD agencies will provide no funding for direct reimbursement of white paper or proposal development costs. NOTE: During any step of the CSO, the Government may send written questions or comments for companies to address via email, or other suitable communication methods as determined by the Government. Benefits of the CSO process and the potential for award include: A streamlined application process requiring only minimal corporate and technical information for fast-track evaluation timelines for solution briefs. Negotiable payment terms for non-dilutive capital. Negotiable intellectual property (IP) rights. Secure and direct feedback from end users, mission partners, and users within the DoD to help product teams develop and hone product design and functionality. Each proposal is evaluated on its individual merits rather than on a comparative basis.
